chapters.title: Chapter 5: Proofs, Pitfalls and Real Choices

lessons.title: Common Salary Structuring Mistakes and Myths

children.text: Every office has a resident tax expert. The colleague who tells you to take the higher CTC, put everything into HRA, never cap your PF, and that gratuity is "your money anyway". Some of that advice was right in 2015. Most of it is wrong in 2026.
This lesson collects the myths that cost Indian salaried professionals the most money, and replaces each with a rule you have already met in this course.

body.text: Most salary structuring mistakes are not maths errors. They are old rules applied to a new regime.

body.caption: What people say, and what is actually true in tax year 2026-27

cells: A higher CTC always means more money
CTC includes employer PF, gratuity and target variable pay. Compare guaranteed cash after tax instead
Put more into HRA and you will save tax
Only in the old regime, and only up to rent minus 10% of basic. HRA above that is fully taxable
Relabel special allowance as LTA or education allowance
In the new regime both are taxed exactly like special allowance. Relabelling saves nothing
Gratuity in my CTC is my money
Permanent employees generally get nothing before 5 years of continuous service
Meal cards and phone bills are too small to matter
Meals, phone and gifts together can take ₹85,800 out of taxable salary, worth ₹26,770 at the 30% slab
Employer NPS is free money, take the maximum
It is deductible but locked until 60, and employer PF plus NPS above ₹7,50,000 a year is taxed
Capping PF at ₹15,000 wages is always better
It raises in-hand but cuts retirement savings and raises taxable salary
The old regime is better because of deductions
Only if your actual exemptions and deductions are large. Otherwise the new regime wins
You cannot claim HRA and home loan interest together
Both can be claimed in the old regime when the facts are genuine, such as renting in the city where you work
I declared my regime to my employer, so I am stuck
Salaried employees without business income can choose the other regime when filing the return
I missed the proof deadline, so my deduction is gone
Genuine old regime claims can still be made in your return. Flexi reimbursements usually cannot
I will return the joining bonus, so the tax will come back
Tax on a repaid bonus is not automatically recovered, especially across tax years
Keep basic low so take-home stays high
Under the Labour Codes special allowance counts as wages, so a thin basic no longer keeps gratuity small
A company car is a perk with no tax
It is a perquisite valued at ₹5,000 or ₹7,000 a month, plus ₹3,000 for a driver

children.text: Two offers from Chapter 1: Company A at ₹16,00,000 fully fixed, and Company B at ₹17,50,000 including ₹3,50,000 of target variable pay, where last year the payout was 70% of target.

body.title: Cash salary after removing employer PF and gratuity

body.text: B pays ₹20,000 more than A only if the payout history repeats, while guaranteeing ₹2,25,000 less. The ₹1.5 lakh higher headline is almost entirely risk transferred to you.

children.text: Myth 2: small components are not worth the paperwork

body.text: These three work in both regimes and need no lock-in, no rent and no children. For most salaried professionals they are the easiest money on the table, and the most commonly ignored.

children.text: Myth 3: the old regime is always better

From Chapter 3: Nisha's ₹20 lakh CTC on her company's default structure cost ₹2,33,950 in the old regime. The same CTC, optimised for the new regime, cost ₹1,14,060. Choosing the old regime without restructuring for it cost her ₹1,19,890 a year.

body.title: When each regime tends to win

columns.label: Old regime can win
points: High rent with a matching HRA component
Home loan interest on a self-occupied house
Two children in school or hostel
Health insurance for self and parents

columns.label: New regime usually wins
points: You live with family or pay low rent
You invest for returns, not for deductions
You want simplicity and fewer proofs

body.title: HRA and home loan together
body.question: Meera works in Bengaluru and pays rent there. She also pays a home loan on a flat in Coimbatore where her parents live. In the old regime, what can she claim?
options: Both HRA and home loan interest, if the facts are genuine
Neither, because claiming both is not allowed
body.explanation: There is no bar on claiming both. HRA covers the rent she actually pays where she works, and home loan interest is claimed on the Coimbatore house. Both must be genuine and documented, and neither is available in the new regime.

children.text: Myth 4: gratuity and PF are simple
: a permanent employee who leaves at 4 years and 11 months generally receives nothing, however many years the CTC showed it.
: deductible up to 14% of basic plus DA, so ₹1,68,000 on a ₹12,00,000 basic, but locked until 60 and counted inside the ₹7,50,000 cap with employer PF.
: raises in-hand today, but in the Chapter 1 example it cut retirement savings by ₹2,44,800 a year and raised taxable salary.
: special allowance now counts as wages, so a thin basic no longer keeps your gratuity small.

body.title: The gratuity rule
body.textWithBlank: A permanent employee generally needs ___ years of continuous service before gratuity becomes payable.
body.explanation: Fixed-term employees qualify after 1 year under the Code on Social Security, 2020, and the service condition does not apply on death or disability. For everyone else, gratuity in a CTC is worth nothing until year 5.

body.title: The small stuff
body.prompt: Rohit is in the 30% slab. He takes a meal card worth ₹52,800, phone reimbursement of ₹18,000 and gift vouchers of ₹15,000 in the year. How much tax does he save, including 4% cess?
body.explanation: ₹85,800 × 31.2% = ₹26,770. All three work in both regimes, so this saving does not depend on his regime, his rent or his investments.

cells: Rent receipts without actual payment
No bank trail, and Form 124 now asks for landlord PAN and your relationship with the landlord
Claim disallowed, plus tax, interest and penalty
Claiming HRA for rent paid to a spouse for a shared home
Not accepted as a genuine tenancy
Claim disallowed
Reimbursement claims without bills
Fixed allowances dressed up as reimbursements
Treated as taxable salary
Not declaring previous employer salary after a job change
Two employers each apply the standard deduction and the lower slabs
Large tax bill plus interest when filing
Claiming deductions in your return that you cannot support
Mismatch with Form 130 and the Annual Information Statement
Notice, and penalty under Section 439 of up to 200% of the tax for misreporting

body.text: The distinction that matters: claiming a genuine deduction your employer refused for want of proof is normal, and you can do it in your return. Manufacturing a claim you cannot support is misreporting, and the penalty is 200% of the tax on it.

body.title: Four pieces of advice from a colleague
body.scenario: Dev, 29, is in the new regime with a ₹16 lakh CTC. A senior colleague tells him: (1) "Ask HR to convert ₹1,00,000 of your special allowance into LTA, it is tax-free." (2) "Cap your PF at ₹1,800 a month, you get more cash." (3) "Never take employer NPS, your money gets stuck." (4) "Skip the meal card, it is only for people who eat in the cafeteria."
body.prompt: Evaluate each piece of advice for Dev.
body.modelAnswer: (1) Wrong for Dev. In the new regime LTA is fully taxable, so this changes nothing except adding a claim process. It would help only if he moved to the old regime and actually travelled in India. (2) Partly true, but incomplete. Capping PF raises in-hand and also raises taxable salary, because the employer's saved contribution usually comes back as taxable special allowance. It is a cash-flow choice, not a tax saving, and it shrinks his retirement corpus. (3) Overstated. Employer NPS is the strongest deduction left in the new regime, up to 14% of basic plus DA. The lock-in is real, so the right answer is a share he can afford to lock away, not zero. (4) Wrong. The meal card is tax-free up to ₹200 per meal in both regimes and is usually accepted at food outlets and delivery apps, not just a cafeteria. If he eats lunch on working days anyway, it is free money. Dev's best moves, in order: meal card, phone reimbursement and gift vouchers, then employer NPS to the extent he can lock money away.

body.title: Myth-buster self-check
steps: Have I compared offers on guaranteed cash after tax, not on CTC?
Am I relabelling components that are fully taxable in my regime?
Do I know the date I complete 5 years for gratuity?
Is my HRA component close to rent minus 10% of basic, if I am in the old regime?
Have I taken the meal, phone and gift components that work in both regimes?
Is my employer PF plus NPS within ₹7,50,000 a year?
Can I prove every claim I make, with bank trails and documents?
Have I rerun the regime comparison on this year's actual numbers?

body.text: Figures refer to tax year 2026-27 and to the examples used earlier in this course. Individual facts change conclusions, particularly on HRA, home loan interest and regime choice. This lesson is for education and is not personalised tax advice.

points: Compare offers on guaranteed cash after tax. Variable pay and gratuity are not guaranteed.
In the new regime, relabelling allowances saves nothing. Only real levers such as employer NPS, meals, phone and perquisite valuations do.
Meal card, phone and gift vouchers can remove ₹85,800 from taxable salary in either regime, worth ₹26,770 at the 30% slab.
The old regime wins only if your genuine exemptions and deductions are large, and only if your structure matches.
HRA and home loan interest can both be claimed in the old regime when the facts are genuine.
Missing proofs is recoverable in your return. Fabricating claims attracts penalties of up to 200% of the tax under Section 439.
